messages:
carmen: heads-up  we rolled a small RBAC tidy to consolidate keystore key labels (mapped `egress-keystore` -> `egress-keystore-v3`) and at the same time applied a TLS cipher tightening in canary. Now seeing widespread mTLS failures for cross-region calls between na and eu. Logs point at KMS unwrap/sign DENY rather than pure cipher negotiation.

lee: any concrete log samples? which key label was requested?

dmitri: paste from proxy-na-11 (na-west):
```
2026-03-26T08:11:02Z proxy-na-11 audit=crypto DENY unwrap key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/egress/cryptoKeys/egress-keystore-v3 labels=[env:prod,region:eu] principal=svc-account:connector-na@dataplane reason=permissionDenied
TLS alert: KEY_UNWRAP_FAILURE
```
downstream: 502 / handshake_fail

carmen: That principal should have been allowed. I think the policy MR changed allowed key resource names and we didn't include label aliases so connectors still request the old label name (egress-keystore) and KMS enforces label->key mapping strictly.

policy-bot: policy-change "keystore-label-consolidation" applied by @carmen at 2026-03-26T08:00:41Z. Runbook: rollback if crypto ops fail.

ops-bot: alert: KMS unwrap/sign DENY spike detected (20 events in 3m) in projects/redwood. Suggested immediate action: validate policy diff and rollback.

lee: Rollback is fastest. Carmen, can you revert the label consolidation while we investigate alias mapping?

carmen: Rolling back now and opening a short change window. Note: this is nastier because caller principals in other regions request the key resource by label; changing canonical key names without alias mappings broke auth flow.

dmitri: While rollback runs, quick mitigation: enable proxy ephemeral CA-caching for 2m to allow in-flight sessions to complete: `kubectl -n proxy annotate deploy/proxy ephemeral-ca-cache=120`

ops-bot: change-window opened by @carmen at 2026-03-26T08:13:10Z for rollback: keystore-label-consolidation -> previous state. recording: changelist-340123.

carmen: rollback applied at 08:14:30 UTC. KMS logs now show unwrap success for previously denied principals. Proxy errors drop to baseline in ~70s.

lee: P0 mitigated. Immediate follow-ups: 1) add a preflight that runs `gcloud kms keys test-iam-permissions` for every principal targeted by the MR (simulate decrypt/sign where applicable) 2) add an audit-alert for KMS DENY unwrap and AsymmetricSign DENY with thresholds (configurable per env) 3) require key-label alias mappings to be present in MR template before label/resource renames are allowed.

dmitri: I'll draft a policy CI job that does a dry-run: it parses the MR for key name changes, enumerates principals with recent KMS activity (via audit logs) and runs testIamPermissions against each region's principal list. It should fail the MR if any principal returns DENY.

sec-oncall: Acknowledged. Opening incident INC-7001 and scheduling 30m RCA. Please attach policy-diff, KMS audit export (08:00-08:20 UTC), and the deploy calendar for the canary window. Also escalate to compliance: simultaneous crypto RBAC and TLS config changes increase blast radius.

carmen: Agreed. action list for RCA: - implement preflight CI check (owner: dmitri) - add key-label alias metadata to keystore keys (owner: lee) - add KMS-deny log-based metrics and pager rules (owner: sec-oncall) - update MR template with explicit alias checklist and a required 24h separation rule between keystore RBAC changes and TLS hardening (owner: policy team)

policy-bot: Incident INC-7001 created and linked to changelist-340123. All artifacts archived.

carmen: final note: treat unwrap vs sign DENY separately in our alert taxonomy because they indicate different failure modes (runtime key access vs certificate issuance). We'll include that in the RCA doc.
